_comment: Six natural Indian complexions for the catalogue. Deliberately NOT strong: the shop sells to a Tamil Nadu audience, so the ladder stays warm-neutral and lightly saturated instead of running to a deep golden/ebony contrast. skinL/skinS are the exact targets tone.py drives every frame to, measured on the saturated upper-third skin cluster with the same definition the audit gate uses. Every tone keeps the SAME saturation band (24-44) so no complexion looks airbrushed or fake-tanned relative to its neighbours.

fair.desc: very fair, cool-neutral light skin, barely warm

light-warm.desc: fair to light, soft warm beige, no orange

light-tan.desc: light tan, natural medium, the catalogue's base complexion

medium-brown.desc: warm medium brown, the most common shade in the market

deep.desc: deep brown, still warm and clear, never muddy

ebony.desc: rich dark brown; the darkest the shop shows, stops short of charcoal

_ladder_checks.note: even 12-18 step ramp; the previous catalogue jumped 48 between light-tan (146.9) and medium-brown (98.1), which made the 6 cards read as 2 groups rather than a ladder
